s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive hip pain with radiating thigh pain and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Progressive left hip pain radiating to the anterior thigh
Antalgic gait and reduced range of motion of the left hip
Synovitis and marrow edema on MRI
key_facts: 1-year history of progressive left hip pain
Pain radiates to the anterior thigh
Pain began as a dull aching groin discomfort
Pain worsened over weeks
Pain is severe at night
Associated with weight loss and anorexia
No history of trauma
Antalgic gait
Reduced range of motion of the left hip in all planes
Tenderness deep in the left groin
Straight-leg raising was negative
Normal neurologic examination
Normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein
Unremarkable pelvic radiograph
MRI showed synovitis and marrow edema without fracture
No clinical improvement with empirical anti-tubercular therapy
Open synovial biopsy showed mild to moderate chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates
Negative cultures and unremarkable rheumatologic evaluation

shortlist.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hip pain and radiating thigh pain with evidence of synovitis and marrow edema on MRI

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Severe night pain, weight loss, and anorexia suggest a possible malignant process

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates on biopsy and joint effusion on MRI

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss and anorexia, and radiographic evidence of a bone lesion

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hip pain and radiating thigh pain with evidence of synovitis and marrow edema on MRI, and lack of response to empirical anti-tubercular therapy

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive hip pain, night pain, and weight loss, along with imaging findings of synovitis, marrow edema, and a well-defined lesion with a sclerotic rim, are consistent with chronic osteomyelitis. The lack of response to anti-tubercular therapy and negative cultures do not rule out this diagnosis, as chronic osteomyelitis can be caused by a variety of organisms and may not always be culture-positive.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Ewing's sarcoma could explain the patient's night pain and weight loss, the imaging findings and biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with joint effusion and synovitis, but the patient's imaging findings and biopsy results suggest a more bone-based process.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: This condition can cause bone lesions, but the patient's age and lack of other systemic symptoms make it less likely.

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While this condition could explain the patient's symptoms, the lack of multiple lesions and the patient's age make it less likely than chronic osteomyelitis.
